title: WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment pipeline parameters
description: Cell segmentation and downstream analysis pipeline for the COMET, MIBI, and OPAL spatial platforms

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to the samplesheet (CSV or YAML) that lists the images to process.
input.help_text: One row per image. Required columns: `sample` and `tiff`. See the Samplesheet page of the documentation for every column.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: The pipeline sends a summary e-mail to this address when the run finishes. You can set it in `~/.nextflow/config` instead of on the command line.

remove_markers.description: Comma-separated channel names to remove from the background-subtracted image. Names are case sensitive.

use_whole_cell_only.description: Use only the whole-cell segmentation to process cells (skip nuclear segmentation).
use_whole_cell_only.help_text: Defaults to `true`: only the whole-cell segmentation is used to process cells. Nuclei are not segmented and nuclear measurements are not produced; cell, erosion, and expansion measurements are kept. Set to `false` to also segment nuclei and measure them.

cell_expansion_microns.description: Grow each cell outward by this distance in µm. 0 turns expansion off.
cell_expansion_microns.help_text:
Each background pixel within this distance of a cell is added to the nearest cell, so growth stops where two cells meet. The distance is converted to pixels with `pixel_size_microns` and rounded (minimum 1 pixel). Use it when the whole-cell masks are nucleus-sized, for example when the nuclear channel is also used as the membrane channel.

Which cells are grown depends on `expand_only_without_membrane` and `use_whole_cell_only`:

- `expand_only_without_membrane = false`, `use_whole_cell_only = true`: every cell is grown.
- `expand_only_without_membrane = false`, `use_whole_cell_only = false`: every whole-cell mask is grown, without growing into nuclei that have no whole-cell mask. Nuclei with no whole-cell mask are then grown by the same distance.
- `expand_only_without_membrane = true` (either `use_whole_cell_only`): nuclei are segmented, and only nuclei with no whole-cell mask are grown. Whole-cell masks are kept as segmented.

When set, it replaces `estimate_cell_boundary_dist`.

expand_only_without_membrane.description: Grow only nuclei that have no whole-cell (membrane) segmentation. Nuclei are segmented for this even when `use_whole_cell_only` is true.
expand_only_without_membrane.help_text:
Cells found by the whole-cell segmentation keep their segmented outline. A nucleus that does not overlap any whole-cell mask is grown by `cell_expansion_microns` to make its cell. This is the approach used by 10x Xenium multimodal cell segmentation. Only used when `cell_expansion_microns` is above 0.

The nuclei come from a separate nuclear segmentation. If `use_whole_cell_only` is true, that segmentation is run anyway and the run logs a warning: every sample is segmented twice, so the run can take up to about twice as long to segment, and nuclear measurements are produced.

combine_channel_options.title: Combine options
combine_channel_options.description: Parameters used for combining membrane channels.

combine_method.description: How to combine several membrane channels into one. `max`: the per-pixel maximum. `norm_mean`: the mean of the channels after rescaling each to its own 50th-99.5th percentile.
combine_method.help_text: Used when `membrane_channels` lists more than one channel. `max` is used by Mesmer, Cellpose and CellSAM. `norm_mean` is used by Cellpose and CellSAM only; a sample that runs Mesmer with `norm_mean` and more than one membrane channel stops the run at startup. With `max`, a dim marker is hidden wherever a brighter marker has signal; `norm_mean` puts every marker on the same scale. See [Combining membrane channels](https://wehi-soda-hub.github.io/sp_segment/background/membrane-channels/).

sopa_options.title: SOPA options
sopa_options.description: Parameters used by SOPA for image patching.

technology.description: Image type for the sopa conversion. Only `ome_tif` is supported.

patch_width_pixel.description: Width and height of each square patch, in pixels, for Cellpose segmentation.

patch_overlap_pixel.description: Overlap between neighbouring patches, in pixels. Set it to at least the diameter of the largest cell.

cellpose_options.title: Cellpose options
cellpose_options.description: Parameters used by Cellpose for the cell segmentation.

cellpose_diameter.description: Expected cell diameter in pixels. Cellpose resizes the image by 30 / diameter before segmentation.
cellpose_diameter.help_text:
Cellpose-SAM models were trained on cell diameters from 7.5 to 120 pixels (mean 30), so the default of 30 suits most data and means no resizing.

- Set the real diameter if your cells are outside 7.5-120 pixels.
- A larger value (for example `90`) shrinks the image and makes the run faster, but small objects are resolved less well.

This parameter does not remove any cells. Use `cellpose_min_area` to remove small objects. A value of `0` means no resizing; Cellpose 4 has no automatic diameter estimate.

cellpose_min_area.description: Discard cells smaller than this many square pixels. Higher keeps fewer cells; 0 keeps every mask.
cellpose_min_area.help_text:
Applied by sopa to each patch during segmentation. The unit is pixels², not µm², so it does not change with `pixel_size_microns`. At 0.28 µm/pixel (COMET), 100 pixels² is 7.8 µm², about a 3.2 µm diameter disc.

`cellsam_min_area` uses the same unit and defaults to 200. `mesmer_min_nuclei_area` is a separate filter on nuclei.

cellpose_flow_threshold.description: Maximum flow error allowed for a mask to be kept. Higher finds more cells, including ill-shaped ones; lower keeps fewer, better-formed ones.
cellpose_flow_threshold.help_text:
Cellpose recomputes the flows each mask implies and compares them with the flows the network predicted. Masks with a mean squared error above this value are removed. This filter acts on shape only.

- Raise it (0.6, 0.8) if visible cells are missing.
- Lower it (0.2, 0.3) if you get ragged, ill-shaped masks.
- `0` turns the check off.

The default 0.4 is Cellpose's default.

cellpose_cellprob_threshold.description: Cutoff on Cellpose's per-pixel cell probability. Lower finds more and larger cells; higher finds fewer and smaller ones.
cellpose_cellprob_threshold.help_text:
Pixels above this value are used to build cells, so it changes which cells are found and where each cell boundary falls. A change here changes cell areas and therefore every per-cell intensity.

The value is not a probability between 0 and 1. It is a logit: the useful range is about -6 to +6, and 0 is the midpoint.

- Lower it (-1, -2) to find faint cells and make cells larger.
- Raise it (1, 2) to stop segmenting background and make cells smaller.

The default 0.0 is Cellpose's default.

cellpose_model_type.description: Retired. Cellpose 4 ignores --model-type; use cellpose_pretrained_model instead.
cellpose_model_type.help_text: Cellpose >=4.0.1 logs `model_type argument is not used in v4.0.1+. Ignoring this argument`, and sopa only reads it on the cellpose<4 code path, so it never had any effect on a v4 run. Setting it now raises an error rather than being silently discarded.

cellpose_pretrained_model.description: Cellpose model to segment with: cpsam_v2 (default), cpsam, cpdino, cpdino-vitb, or a path to a custom model.
cellpose_pretrained_model.help_text:
Built-in models (cellpose 4.2.1.1):

- `cpsam_v2`: default; the current Cellpose-SAM model.
- `cpsam`: the previous Cellpose-SAM model. Use it to reproduce results from before cellpose 4.2.
- `cpdino`: DINOv3 backbone (ViT-L).
- `cpdino-vitb`: smaller DINOv3 backbone (ViT-B).

Any other value is treated as a path to a custom model and must exist; the pipeline checks this at startup. Built-in models are downloaded once per run, or read from `cellpose_models_dir` if set. See CITATIONS.md for the DINOv3 licence terms.

cellpose_models_dir.description: Directory holding pre-staged Cellpose model weights. If set, the pipeline uses it instead of downloading them.
cellpose_models_dir.help_text: A directory that holds the Cellpose model cache (for example a `cpsam_v2` file). Use it when compute nodes have no internet access. The directory must exist and must not be under `/opt`.

cellpose_preprocessing_options.title: Cellpose preprocessing options
cellpose_preprocessing_options.description: Intensity preprocessing applied before Cellpose segmentation.
cellpose_preprocessing_options.help_text: The defaults make the pipeline match Cellpose's own preprocessing: rescale each patch to its 1st and 99th percentiles and nothing else. sopa's gaussian filter and CLAHE are turned off. To restore sopa's behaviour, set `cellpose_clip_limit` to 0.2 and `cellpose_gaussian_sigma` to 1. See the Cellpose preprocessing page of the documentation for the measurements behind these defaults.

cellpose_tile_norm_blocksize.description: Block size in pixels for Cellpose's tile-local intensity normalisation. 0 uses Cellpose's whole-patch default.
cellpose_tile_norm_blocksize.help_text:
When greater than 0, Cellpose computes the 1st/99th percentiles separately for each block of this size inside the patch instead of once for the whole patch.

Use a block much larger than a cell. At 0.28 µm/pixel, 512 pixels is 143 µm (about 17 nuclear diameters). Small blocks (for example 128 pixels) can contain no nuclei in sparse tissue; their noise is then stretched to the full intensity range and results get worse.

cellpose_clip_limit.description: sopa's CLAHE clip limit, applied before Cellpose. Defaults to 0 in this pipeline, disabling CLAHE; null restores sopa's default of 0.2.
cellpose_clip_limit.help_text: sopa applies CLAHE (`skimage.exposure.equalize_adapthist`) to each patch before Cellpose. Cellpose itself has no CLAHE step and its models were not trained with it. `0` turns CLAHE off. With CLAHE on, results change with `patch_width_pixel`, because the CLAHE kernel size is derived from the patch size.

cellpose_clahe_kernel_size.description: Kernel size in pixels for sopa's CLAHE. Unset uses skimage's default of patch.shape // 8, which scales with patch_width_pixel.
cellpose_clahe_kernel_size.help_text: If unset, skimage uses 1/8 of the patch height and width: 375 pixels at `patch_width_pixel` 3000. Setting a fixed value stops the kernel size changing with the patch size. Has no effect while `cellpose_clip_limit` is 0.

cellpose_gaussian_sigma.description: Sigma for sopa's gaussian smoothing, applied before Cellpose. Defaults to 0 in this pipeline, disabling it; null restores sopa's default of 1.
cellpose_gaussian_sigma.help_text: sopa applies a gaussian filter to each patch before Cellpose. Cellpose applies no smoothing by default. `0` turns the filter off. Raise it only if your images are noisy enough to need smoothing before segmentation.

mesmer_options.title: Mesmer options
mesmer_options.description: Parameters used by the MesmerSegmentation tool.

mesmer_segmentation_level.description: Segmentation level passed to Mesmer as `--segmentation-level` (legacy option). Unset by default.

mesmer_maxima_threshold.description: Mesmer maxima threshold. Lower values give more cells; higher values give fewer cells.

mesmer_interior_threshold.description: Mesmer interior threshold. Higher values give smaller nuclei and cells.

mesmer_maxima_smooth.description: Smoothing applied to Mesmer's maxima signal. Higher values give more regular shapes.

mesmer_min_nuclei_area.description: Minimum nucleus area in pixels². Smaller nuclei are removed by Mesmer.

mesmer_remove_border_cells.description: Remove cells that touch the image border.

mesmer_pixel_expansion.description: Number of pixels to expand each Mesmer cell after segmentation.

mesmer_padding.description: Number of pixels to crop from each side of the image before Mesmer segmentation.

mesmer_transpose_mask.description: Transpose the Mesmer output mask. Enable this only if the mask is flipped relative to the image.

cellsam_options.title: CellSAM options
cellsam_options.description: Parameters used by CellSAM for foundation model cell segmentation.

cellsam_bbox_threshold.description: Confidence threshold for CellSAM cell detections. Lower values (0.3-0.4) find more cells on images unlike the training data.

cellsam_block_size.description: Tile size in pixels for whole-slide CellSAM processing.

cellsam_overlap.description: Overlap between CellSAM tiles, in pixels. Set it to at least the typical cell diameter.

cellsam_iou_depth.description: Distance in pixels searched for duplicate cells at tile boundaries.

cellsam_iou_threshold.description: IoU above which two overlapping cells at a tile boundary are merged.

cellsam_use_wsi.description: Process the image in tiles (whole-slide mode). Required for large images.

cellsam_gauge_cell_size.description: Run a first CellSAM pass to estimate cell size before segmentation.

cellsam_low_contrast_enhancement.description: Apply contrast enhancement before segmentation, for low-contrast images.

cellsam_model_path.description: Path to custom CellSAM model weights. If unset, the CellSAM generalist model is used (v1.2 when `DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN` is set).

cellsam_min_area.description: Remove cells smaller than this many pixels². `0` keeps every cell.
cellsam_min_area.help_text:
CellSAM counts each cell's pixels and applies the filter once, after the tiles are merged. The unit is pixels², not µm². At 0.28 µm/pixel, 200 pixels² is 15.7 µm². Cells with an area equal to the threshold are kept.

`cellpose_min_area` measures the area of the cell polygon instead. On test cells the polygon area was 0.93-1.00 times the pixel count (median 0.99), so at the same value the two filters remove almost the same cells. `cellpose_min_area` defaults to 100.

cellsam_remove_border_cells.description: Remove CellSAM cells that touch the image edge.
cellsam_remove_border_cells.help_text: Cells cut by the image edge are incomplete, so they are removed by default. Set to `false` to keep them.

kronos_options.title: KRONOS2 embedding options
kronos_options.description: Options for KRONOS2 per-cell foundation-model embeddings
kronos_options.help_text: KRONOS2 is a foundation model for multiplex spatial proteomics. These parameters control the optional step that adds a 768-value embedding to every cell after cell measurement.

enable_kronos.help_text: Set to `true` to compute KRONOS2 embeddings after cell measurement. Requires `kronos_model_path`.

kronos_model_path.description: Path to a full KRONOS2 snapshot directory, or a Hugging Face repo id.
kronos_model_path.help_text:
Request access to `MahmoodLab/KRONOS2` on Hugging Face, then download the full snapshot:

`hf download MahmoodLab/KRONOS2 --local-dir /path/to/KRONOS2 --exclude "demo_image/*"`

A partial download does not work, because the loader imports the `dinov2` package bundled in the snapshot. Do not store the snapshot under `/opt`.

kronos_patch_size.description: Size of cell-centered patches to extract for KRONOS inference.
kronos_patch_size.help_text: Side length in pixels of the square patch centred on each cell. Larger patches include more surrounding tissue and take longer.

kronos_batch_size.description: Batch size for inference. KRONOS2 runs fp32 and cuBLAS picks batch-dependent kernels, so this shifts embeddings slightly; 16 reproduces the published values.
kronos_batch_size.help_text: Number of cell patches per GPU batch. Larger batches are faster and use more GPU memory. Embeddings change very slightly with batch size; 16 reproduces the published values.

kronos_num_workers.description: Number of parallel DataLoader workers for loading and preprocessing cell patches.
kronos_num_workers.help_text: Number of CPU processes that read and prepare patches while the GPU runs. `0` reads in the main process. Set it to the number of CPUs allocated to the task.

kronos_max_value.description: Override the intensity divisor. Unset derives it from the image dtype (uint8=255, uint16=65535, float=400), matching KRONOS2 itself.

kronos_marker_mapping.description: JSON file, or an inline JSON object, that maps channel names to KRONOS2 marker names, e.g. {"Collagen 4": "COLLAGENiv"}.
kronos_marker_mapping.help_text:
KRONOS2 matches marker names exactly, ignoring separators (`CD-8`, `CD_8` and `CD8` match). There is no alias or fuzzy matching, so a spelling variant such as `Cytokeritin` does not match `CYTOKERATIN`. The run fails if any channel does not match, unless `kronos_allow_novel_defaults` is `true`.

The mapping changes only the names given to KRONOS2. Channel names in the image and the GeoJSON are not changed. A value that is neither an existing file nor valid JSON fails the run.

kronos_exclude_markers.description: Comma-separated channel names that KRONOS2 does not read, e.g. 'Autofluorescence'. Other steps still use these channels.
kronos_exclude_markers.help_text:
Use it for channels that are not markers: autofluorescence, blanks, empty cycles. The channel stays in the image and keeps its cell measurements.

- Names are case sensitive and are matched against the image's channel names before `kronos_marker_mapping` is applied.
- A name that matches no channel fails the run.
- The nuclear channel cannot be excluded.
- Excluding a channel changes every cell's embedding. Use the same list for every image in a cohort.

kronos_nuclear_marker.description: Channel that KRONOS2 treats as its DAPI channel. Defaults to the samplesheet `nuclear_channel`.

kronos_isolate_cell.description: Zero pixels outside the target cell so each embedding describes that cell rather than its surrounding neighbourhood.

kronos_allow_novel_defaults.description: Continue when a channel name is not in the KRONOS2 vocabulary. That channel is normalised with default statistics. Off by default, so the run fails instead.

measurement_options.title: Cell measurement options
measurement_options.help_text: Parameters for the cell measurement step (cellmeasurement-py).

enable_measurements.help_text: Set to `false` to skip intensity and shape measurements. Cell outlines are still written to the GeoJSON. Skipping saves time on large images.

percentiles.description: Comma-separated list of percentiles to calculate for each marker (e.g. 80,90,95,99).
percentiles.help_text: Each value must be between 0 and 100. Requires `enable_measurements` to be `true`.

erosion_steps.description: Measure intensity in 5 equal-area erosion bins working inward from the cell/nucleus boundary.
erosion_steps.help_text: Splits each cell (and nucleus) into 5 rings of approximately equal area, from the boundary inward, and measures mean and median intensity in each ring. Requires `enable_measurements` to be `true`.

expansion_steps.description: Measure intensity in 5 equal-area annular bins dilated 20 µm outward from the cell boundary (distance computed from pixel_size_microns).
expansion_steps.help_text: Splits the 20 µm zone outside each cell into 5 rings of approximately equal area and measures mean and median intensity in each ring. The distance in pixels is computed from `pixel_size_microns`. Requires `enable_measurements` to be `true`.

environment_expansion.description: Measure a 20 µm pericellular 'Environment' compartment (distance computed automatically from pixel_size_microns).
environment_expansion.help_text: Measures mean, median, min, max and standard deviation of every channel in the zone from the cell boundary to 20 µm outside it, as one region (`Environment_20um`). The distance in pixels is computed from `pixel_size_microns`.

estimate_cell_boundary_dist.description: For a nucleus with no matching whole-cell ROI, expand the nucleus by this many pixels to make the cell. Ignored when `cell_expansion_microns` is above 0.

neighbors.description: Number of nearest neighbours used for neighbourhood features. `0` turns them off.
neighbors.help_text: For each cell, the mean of every numeric measurement over its nearest neighbours (up to this number, within 20 µm of the cell centroid) is added as `Neighbours: Mean: <measurement>`. Typical values: 5-10.

gzip_geojson.description: Gzip-compress the output GeoJSON files. Produces .geojson.gz instead of .geojson.
gzip_geojson.help_text: Writes `.geojson.gz` instead of `.geojson`. Whole-slide GeoJSON files can exceed 100 GB uncompressed; gzip usually reduces them 10-20 times. The import_large_geojson pipeline reads the compressed files directly.

dist_threshold.description: Maximum centroid distance in pixels for matching a nucleus to a whole-cell ROI.
dist_threshold.help_text: A nucleus and a whole-cell ROI whose centroids are further apart than this are not matched. Unmatched nuclei get a cell boundary made by expanding the nucleus (see `estimate_cell_boundary_dist`).

downsample_factor.description: Downsample factor applied to the image and masks before measurement (1 = no downsampling).
downsample_factor.help_text: An integer of 2 or more downsamples the image (block mean) and masks (block max) before measurement. Values below 2 mean no downsampling. Area and length measurements are scaled back to full-resolution units.

tile_size.description: Tile size for large image measurement calculations.
tile_size.help_text: Measurements are computed on tiles in parallel. Aim for 2-4 times more tiles than CPUs.

tile_overlap.description: Tile overlap region in pixels. Should encompass typical cell size.
tile_overlap.help_text: Set it to at least the diameter of the largest cell, so every cell is complete in at least one tile.

geometry_checkpoint_dir.help_text: Each completed batch of cell polygons is written here, so a CELLMEASUREMENT task that is killed resumes from the last completed batch. The directory must be outside the Nextflow work directory. Checkpoints are not deleted automatically. Leave unset to turn checkpointing off.

geometry_batch_size.description: Cells per polygon-extraction batch, and the checkpoint granularity.
geometry_batch_size.help_text: Smaller batches are checkpointed more often but add overhead. A killed task loses at most one batch per worker.

report_options.title: Report options
report_options.description: Parameters used for segmentation report generation.
report_options.help_text: Parameters for the segmentation QC report.

generate_report.help_text: Set to `true` to write an HTML QC report per sample. The report is most complete when `enable_measurements` is `true`.

mask_smoothing_options.title: Mask smoothing options
mask_smoothing_options.description: Parameters for optional mask smoothing before cell measurement.
mask_smoothing_options.help_text: Enable mask smoothing to reduce polygon complexity in segmentation masks. This can prevent StackOverflowError in QuPath's GeoJSON export when cell ROIs have overly complex/jagged boundaries.

smooth_masks.description: Enable mask smoothing before cell measurement.
smooth_masks.help_text: Smooths the label masks before cell measurement to reduce the number of polygon vertices. Use it if QuPath fails with StackOverflowError when exporting or loading the GeoJSON. Choose the method with `smooth_method`.

smooth_method.description: Smoothing algorithm: 'morphological' (disk close+open) or 'shapely' (Douglas-Peucker polygon simplification).
smooth_method.help_text: `morphological` applies a binary close then open with a disk of radius `smooth_kernel_size`. `shapely` simplifies each cell outline with the Douglas-Peucker algorithm (tolerance `smooth_tolerance`), which reduces the vertex count directly.

smooth_kernel_size.description: Disk radius in pixels for `morphological` smoothing.
smooth_kernel_size.help_text: Larger values give smoother outlines but can merge neighbouring cells.

smooth_n_workers.description: Number of worker processes for mask smoothing.
smooth_n_workers.help_text: Set it to the number of CPUs allocated to the SMOOTHMASKS task.

smooth_chunksize.description: Number of labels each smoothing worker processes at a time.
smooth_chunksize.help_text: Use larger values for many small cells and smaller values for fewer large cells.

smooth_tolerance.description: Douglas-Peucker tolerance in pixels for `shapely` smoothing.
smooth_tolerance.help_text: Higher values give simpler outlines with fewer vertices. Start with 1.

smooth_min_area.description: Minimum polygon area in pixels² kept after `shapely` smoothing.
smooth_min_area.help_text: Removes fragments created by simplification. `0` keeps every cell.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

hook_url.description: Incoming hook URL for messaging service
hook_url.help_text: Incoming hook URL for messaging service. Currently, MS Teams and Slack are supported.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

deepcell_cache_dir.description: Base directory for caching DeepCell/CellSAM model weights. The current username is appended automatically.
deepcell_cache_dir.help_text: Set this to redirect the DeepCell model cache away from the home directory. The current username is resolved at runtime and appended, so models are cached at {deepcell_cache_dir}/{username}/.deepcell/models/. Set to null to use $HOME instead.

container_cache_dir.description: Directory for the Apptainer/Singularity image cache. Set this on any cluster where $HOME has a quota.
container_cache_dir.help_text: Sets apptainer.cacheDir and singularity.cacheDir, so converted .img files are written here rather than under the work directory. This covers only half of a pull: Apptainer unpacks the OCI layers it converts from into $APPTAINER_CACHEDIR (default ~/.apptainer/cache), which Nextflow cannot set because it pulls images from its own process rather than from a task. Export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR and SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR to the same filesystem before launching; the pipeline errors at startup if this parameter is set without them.
